hints: Picture where each part sits on a chromosome. P1 is in the middle constriction, P3 is right at the tips, and P2 proteins are found all along the DNA.
Now match the job to the position. Which job needs packaging all along the DNA, which needs joining in the middle, and which needs protecting the ends from being worn away?
walkthrough:
**Sort out what each part is**

Think of a duplicated chromosome like an X shape. P1, the centromere, is the pinched waist in the middle. P3, the telomere, means end, so it is the cap at each tip. P2, histone proteins, are the tiny spools that DNA winds around all along its length.

**Match each part to its true job**

Histones (P2) package the long DNA molecule into compact nucleosomes, so P2 matches F1. The centromere (P1) is where the two sister chromatids are held together, so P1 matches F2. The telomeres (P3) are repeated non-coding sequences that protect the ends during replication, so genes are not lost, so P3 matches F3.

**Pick the correct pairing**

Only one option in the list gives a true pair. P3 with F3 correctly links telomere with prevents loss of genes. That is option D.

options.A: P1 is the centromere, not the packaging protein. Packaging DNA into compact structures (F1) is the job of histone proteins (P2).
options.B: P1 is the centromere which holds chromatids together (F2). Preventing loss of genes (F3) is the protective role of the telomere at the chromosome ends.
options.C: P2 histone proteins package DNA (F1), they do not join chromatids. Holding two chromatids together (F2) is the job of the centromere (P1).
options.D: Well done, this is correct. P3 telomeres cap the chromosome ends with repeated DNA, so a little is lost each division without losing important genes (F3).
